channel.title: Random Comics
channel.description: Standalone comics, strange experiments, one-shot adventures, spontaneous comic ideas, and future comic series.

item.title: The Soulforge Knight
item.description: After a Far Lands dragon destroys a thousand royal knights and kidnaps the princess, an anxious old wizard raises their molten armor and loyal spirits into a giant super knight who must choose sacrifice over survival. Issue #5 of Superhero Action Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: Guardian Angels Of Earth
item.description: The Demon King emerges immortal, and Marcus must combine Faith Force, Divine Fire, and Gaia Green to destroy him before Earth splits apart. Issue #4 of Faith Force. 8 pages.

item.title: Manager Of Monsters
item.description: A mall store manager gets lost in an impossible storage room where monsters obey workplace rules, only to become their king and fall when he forgets the ordinary life that gave him power. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Sky Iron Harvest
item.description: When a rusting android abducts Atlas with a heart of Sky Iron, New York's own Big Apple must track the weakness signal, storm the warehouse, and save the world's strongest hero with a sprinkler pipe and an apple from his belt. Issue #4 of Superhero Action Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: Armor Fed By Hell
item.description: When a surviving cultist uses Hell-powered armor to overpower the world's armies, Marcus learns to focus Faith Force into a concentrated blast. Issue #2 of Faith Force. 8 pages.

item.title: Stained Glass Souls
item.description: After a soul-thief wizard traps Super Cowboy inside a stained-glass church window and steals a little girl's spirit, Super Cowboy turns his shame into a search through the spirit world and frees every soul powering the wizard's magic. Issue #3 of Super Cowboy. 8 pages.

item.title: The God Tree Ultimatum
item.description: A rogue angel plants a world-killing God Tree to stop the Demon King, forcing Marcus to wield Earth's stolen life-force as Gaia Green energy. Issue #3 of Faith Force. 8 pages.

item.title: The Portal That Would Not Close
item.description: Earth's greatest martial artists interrupt a cult's Hell portal ritual when Marcus Hale's faith in his team ignites the golden aura of Faith Force. Issue #1 of Faith Force. 8 pages.

item.title: Lightning Rode With Me
item.description: After a triumphant Light Lasso swing across Dustfall, Super Cowboy returns to the Dustfall Sheriff Office and remembers the stormy night the lasso found him and turned a doomed desert crossing into the start of his heroic life. Issue #2 of Super Cowboy. 8 pages.

item.title: I Called Your Bluff
item.description: Super Cowboy must stop a steam-driven robotic outlaw from stealing Dustfall's gold by calling the machine's self-destruct bluff and trusting the Light Lasso under brutal pressure. Issue #1 of Super Cowboy. 8 pages.

item.title: The God Who Turned Away
item.description: Radiant Vector races into the past to preserve magic for all humanity, only to witness the fall of Atlantis and decide that unlimited power would destroy the world he hoped to save. Issue #3 of Superhero Action Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: The Place Between Worlds
item.description: Queen Amazoness reaches the Universal Nexus and questions how a floating wilderness can become a school, while Princess Amazoness turns Lysandra's failed challenge into the first test of a more open crown. Issue #5 of Starborn Sisters. 8 pages.

item.title: Through the Broken Belt
item.description: Queen Amazoness and Princess Veyla survive an asteroid field by joining tactical knowledge with alien piloting, while Princess Amazoness reaches home only to be attacked by Lysandra for a crown she does not even want. Issue #4 of Starborn Sisters. 8 pages.

item.title: Keep It Steady
item.description: Sasha faces the reality-eating incursion with almost no training and discovers that her borrowed power only works when she stops performing heroism and learns to hold steady. Issue #3 of Nexus Nights. 8 pages.

item.title: Seeds Above the Shore
item.description: Princess Veyla turns Queen Amazoness's lesson into a sky battle, using thorns, seeds, and poison in the blood to defeat Commander Grax Vorn without becoming the kind of conqueror he serves. Issue #2 of Starborn Sisters. 8 pages.

item.title: Small Hand Wiggles
item.description: Sasha suits up for her one-night hero mission, receives a rushed lesson in Astral Manipulation, and is deployed toward a reality-eating incursion before training can become anything more than "small hand wiggles." Issue #2 of Nexus Nights. 8 pages.

item.title: The First Starfall
item.description: Before Starborn Academy exists, Queen Amazoness shelters an alien princess whose pursuit by the Galactic Empire turns Earth's hidden island into the first lesson of an interstellar heroic future. Issue #1 of Starborn Sisters. 8 pages.

item.title: The Teacher's Crown
item.description: Princess Veyla asks Queen Amazoness to teach the galaxy instead of waging war, forcing Amazoness to choose a future beyond the island and provoking her advisor's warrior-first challenge to the crown. Issue #3 of Starborn Sisters. 8 pages.

item.title: Tourist Processing
item.description: Sasha arrives in Nexus City expecting a thrilling one-night superhero adventure, but Astral Command's power activation process teaches her that paid hero tourism can be lethal before the mission even begins. Issue #1 of Nexus Nights. 8 pages.

item.title: False Hunger
item.description: Cornered by a starving corrupted bandit who could kill them with one punch, the Guardians must save her without letting compassion become hesitation. Issue #4 of Wild Zone Guardians. 8 pages.

item.title: No Time To Rest
item.description: After the first anomaly cleansing, the Chronicler learns why the exhausted Wild Zone Guardians cannot simply rest, and a starving corrupted bandit turns the lesson into a cliffhanger. Issue #3 of Wild Zone Guardians. 8 pages.

item.title: Off-World Observer
item.description: The Chronicler arrives in a regulated tech-magic city to find real superhero stories, but their illegal teleporter forces them into temporary observer status and points them toward the dangerous Wild Zones. Issue #1 of Wild Zone Guardians. 8 pages.

item.title: Reality Breakers Recap
item.description: Jack Blue breaks the fourth wall to give readers a complete catch-up issue covering the Reality Breakers' origin, powers, personalities, motivations, major victories, and current story status. Issue #5 of Super School RPG CAI Adaptation. 8 pages.

item.title: The First Cleansing
item.description: The Chronicler follows Kaelen and Vessara to their first active anomaly site, where a corrupted crystal beast forces them to become more than an observer by inventing the Tele-Shot. Issue #2 of Wild Zone Guardians. 8 pages.

item.title: Gravity Redemption
item.description: The Reality Breakers survive their first moments in Shadowgarde City by protecting civilians and persuading a rogue gravity student to stand down before Shadowgarde's own responders arrive. Issue #4 of Super School RPG CAI Adaptation. 8 pages.

item.title: Lava Leviathan Co-Op
item.description: Jack Blue follows Miss Aurora into the Simulation Dome and turns Blaze Carter's fiery rivalry into a coordinated team victory over a molten holographic monster. Issue #2 of Super School RPG CAI Adaptation. 8 pages.

item.title: Shadowgarde Field Trip
item.description: After the Simulation Dome names Jack, Aurora, and Blaze the Reality Breakers, Professor Lightman sends them on their first real Field Trip mission to stop a gravity crisis in Shadowgarde City. Issue #3 of Super School RPG CAI Adaptation. 8 pages.

item.title: The Cosmic Debut
item.description: Jack Blue joins Super School Class 1A, humbly asks to be treated like an ordinary student, demonstrates breathtaking control over cosmic reality warping, and reveals that he observes their world through an interdimensional chat window. Issue #1 of Super School RPG CAI Adaptation. 8 pages.

item.title: Crystal Hell
item.description: After Hell Queen's crystal prison power turns addictive, the teenage superhero team that once helped the world accept her must stop her without killing the friend they still believe can come home. Issue #2 of Superhero Action Comics. 9 pages.

item.title: Body of Fire
item.description: Mister Titanic enters a collapsing burning building to save trapped survivors, only to discover that a fire elemental staged the disaster to bait a hero into battle. Issue #1 of Superhero Action Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: The Spinach Sailor Rescue
item.description: Pop The Imp jumps into the book "Spinach Sailor" and turns himself into the one thing his reluctant sailor partner needs to rescue a kidnapped girlfriend: hyperreality spinach. Issue #1 of Pop The Imp. 8 pages.

item.title: Probably Dreaming: Fangs for the Dream
item.description: Dracula sneaks into Jet Black's apartment before dawn to drink his blood, but Jet treats the attack like a lucid dream challenge and accidentally defeats the vampire with dream-faith, practical violence, and morning sunlight. Issue #2 of Probably Dreaming. 8 pages.

item.title: The Dark Magic Candy Golem
item.description: Two retired legendary warriors arrive on Candy Island for peace, only to defeat their enemies' regenerating candy golem by discovering the one thing it cannot recover from: being eaten. Issue #1 of Sugarblade & Starfang. 8 pages.

item.title: Probably Dreaming: Bite Me at 4:30
item.description: Jet Black assumes a zombie at his apartment door is proof that he is dreaming, so he becomes a zombie on purpose and treats the apocalypse as a boring Lucid Light problem until Huntsville mysteriously resets. Issue #1 of Probably Dreaming. 9 pages.

item.title: The Selfish Wish
item.description: Rann Dominique selfishly wishes for superpowers, unleashes an alien prison, dies, and returns from Limbo with unstable powers and one chance to save Earth. Issue #1 of Power Flux. 8 pages.

item.title: Trigger Discipline
item.description: A reckless laser-tag player dreams into a utopian laser city under drone attack and learns that smart cover, timing, and patience beat charging straight into the fight. Issue #2 of Storyverse Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: Past Due Miracle
item.description: After Second Skin fails against the Immortal Curse, Adam Frankenstein takes God's first repo job and reclaims stolen Lucid Light from a fake miracle preacher. Issue #1 of Divine Repo. 9 pages.

item.title: The God That Wasn't
item.description: After his sister leaves the swamp, Wes follows a demon-fed fairy tale to the edge of reality and mistakes a cosmic horror's awakening for divine salvation. Issue #1 of Quest Series. 9 pages.

item.title: The Map That Feared the Ending
item.description: An anxious young mapmaker dreams into Inkfall Reef and must help a Dream Guardian trap a Nightmare that feeds on her fear of choosing the wrong ending. Issue #1 of Storyverse Comics. 8 pages.

item.title: Captain Galaxy: The Living Castle
item.description: When the living Cosmic Castle reveals that Captain Galaxy has only ever been its disposable host, the frightened hero must decide whether to accept the doomed Storyverse or prove his courage by shielding every story from a universe-ending flood. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Channel Zero
item.description: A midnight lightning strike bonds local access technician Bob Carlson to a cosmic remote, forcing him to cast forgotten story-forms against a Nightmare static kaiju. Issue #1 of Dream Caster. 8 pages.

item.title: Backrooms Lucid Light
item.description: Lucid dreamer Jet Black falls through his own couch into the Backrooms, loses access to his purple Lucid Light, and survives a hunting mimic crate by turning the Backrooms' no-clipping logic against itself. Standalone issue. 9 pages.

item.title: Nothing Special
item.description: Rejected at birth for having no Hacks, Genny Manson turns the world's most ignored power into the first proof that he can become a hero. Issue #1 of Generic Man. 8 pages.

item.title: Spark of Lucid Light
item.description: After a global event called the Spark gives some people fantastic abilities and makes them targets, Jet Black discovers his dream power is real when a government capture robot tears him from his apartment and forces him to choose between hiding and joining the resistance. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Anamorphis UAP
item.description: A drained comic-book creator sees a blurry leaked military video of a luminous faceless being and chooses to turn that disputed evidence into art that helps people look for wonder again. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: The Battery Problem
item.description: Dark Light's one-soldier-at-a-time hunt across the Storyverse exposes the difference between temporary Lucid Dreamers and rare native Lucid Conduits, turning King Kaine Chester into an unavoidable target. Issue #3 of The Three Hands. 8 pages.

item.title: The King's Three Hands
item.description: Kaine tests his kingdom's strongest defenders against hardlight Anamorphis simulations and learns that the right Three Hands must be knights who can harm light, keep choosing the fight, and still trust the king he once was. Issue #4 of The Three Hands. 8 pages.

item.title: The Limits of Lucid Light
item.description: Before warning Kaine's island city, the Lucid Lord returns to his rigid homeworld to prove his worth, only to discover that even Lucid Light cannot rewrite a story already locked under Dark Light's rule. Issue #2 of The Three Hands. 8 pages.

item.title: The Promise of Lucid Light
item.description: King Kaine Chester's island city nears rebellion under his corrupted Lucid Light rule until the Lucid Lord cleanses him and warns that a greater darkness is coming for his power. Issue #1 of The Three Hands. 8 pages.

item.title: N-7: The Hoax File
item.description: When Anonymous releases a buried 1994 contact file about N-7, a non-human feline humanoid recovered at the Nevada Test and Training Range, the world calls it a hoax. The leak argues that the hoax story was built to hide the only witness who told the truth. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: The Dark Above
item.description: After a late superhero movie, a wealthy family's shortcut through a neglected alley becomes an origin story for something predatory when their young son discovers flight, fangs, and a hunger that spreads. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: The Section 10 Files
item.description: After UFO disclosure files coincide with a wave of vanished scientists, an Anonymous cell digs through nearly 200 releases and discovers the disappearances point to shapeshifting "Dark Clothed Creatures," forcing the hackers to seek psychic contact with Master Kalen-Li and the hidden Korrendorian guardians of Earth. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Bun-Bun and the Lightless God
item.description: When ash from a volcanic eruption starves a stranded Valordian crew of sunlight, their youngest explorer steals sacred ore from a cave god's shrine and survives only by turning her flight field into a desperate act of escape. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Figure Fiddler: Dust Demon
item.description: A blocked writer named Toby slips into an action-figure daydream where his cluttered office becomes a besieged toy city, and only a holy hoverbike built from a handheld vacuum can save his corrupted collection from a Dust Demon. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Particle Patriot: Time Displacement
item.description: On an early government mission, a quantum superhero made of red, white, and blue atoms must escape the Jurassic past and a ruined future to stop Clocktor before one stolen moment becomes a permanent empire. Standalone issue. 8 pages.

item.title: Deca-Form: Island Retirement
item.description: After a supernatural storm destroys his cruise ship, Deca-Form must stop treating survival as a rescue mission and use his alien transformations to build a new life on an empty island. Standalone issue. 9 pages.
